cells.tense: You are handing on something this group has found worth keeping, and it still travels through you.
cells.ask: Give one piece of what you know to someone who didn't ask, in words small enough to survive a careless retelling.
cells.core:
The whole shape is legible to you — who is holding what, where it's shifting, which seams are load-bearing. So what you pass along gets taken up, even when your voice isn't the loudest one in the room. You know why the thing matters, and that knowing is what keeps it from hardening into a rule.

A custom stays alive by moving through someone who can bend it without breaking it. The test isn't how faithfully you reproduce it; it's whether it can travel once you've stood up and gone. This week, hand one piece to someone who never asked, simplified until it can survive being repeated wrong. Then leave it with them. What gets handed on is what keeps going.

cells.tense: You are policing a custom against a change that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Choose one rule you enforce. Skip it once, and watch whether what it protects actually collapses.
cells.core:
You're reading the room clearly and guarding the edges harder than anyone asked. Every version gets measured against the correct one. Every person gets quietly checked for whether they hold it right. The windows are closing and you're the one drawing them shut.

What has proven valuable survives because it can shift without snapping. What you're doing instead is bracing it against a change still in the future, and the bracing is losing the thing it was meant to save. Nothing sealed has stayed alive inside the seal. This week, pick one rule you enforce and leave it unenforced once. Watch what actually happens. If the old thing is real, it holds through a day of your hands off it.

cells.tense: You stopped standing inside a lineage a while back, and you haven't said where.
cells.ask: Ask one person where they got what they believe. Listen for what's old in it, and name what you recognized.
cells.core:
The whole shape is legible to you, but you're a visitor inside it. Nothing behind you arrives as yours to carry, so every insight you reach gets built from nothing. You re-derive, alone, what other people were handed down.

Reading patterns isn't the problem. A reading with nothing behind it runs on your own supply, and the supply shows. Nobody handed you anything, so nothing holds you when looking gets tiring. This week, ask one person where they got what they believe. Don't debate it, don't grade it. Find the chain behind their answer, and name what in it you already recognized. That's the closed door you've been standing at.

cells.tense: You are already passing something on to the people around you and you have not claimed it.
cells.ask: Say one sentence to someone about what you're handing on, plainly in your own name — call it yours.
cells.core:
What you say from this vantage — what you tell people, what you let stand, what you decide is worth saying at all — goes out and leaves the room with them. You'd call it just talking. The handing on is already running. Whoever is doing it hasn't signed.

This works better when you own it. What has proven valuable moves through someone who knows they're holding it; right now it moves through someone insisting they're only standing there. This week, say one sentence to someone about what you're handing on, in your own name. Not a lesson. A claim. The rest adjusts around that.
